correctness.rationale: Solved the coupled backward Laplace equations using stationary gate mean F and difference W. The exact transform is 1/[cosh(sqrt u)+q sqrt u sinh(sqrt u)*h(z+u)], z=(alpha+beta)L^2/D, q=beta/alpha, h(z)=coth(sqrt z)/sqrt z. Expansion yields m=1/2+q h(z), v=m^2-m/3+1/12-2(m-1/2)h'(z)/h(z). The Mittag-Leffler expansion of h as an integral of a strictly positive Laplace kernel makes (log h)' strictly increasing from -infinity to 0. Therefore every datum in the strict feasible half-region has exactly one z, q, and pair of positive rates. Independently tested rate reconstruction and moment floor for multiple parameter choices, with independent backward boundary-matrix checks in the inspected package. The inequality is strict at any finite positive rate.

originality.rationale: Rate inference from full gated first-passage distributions and short-time detection tails was established by Kumar-Scher-Reuveni-Santhanam (2023), and forward gated diffusion moment transforms by Bressloff-Lawley/Bressloff. The inspected Kumar author-preprint main text and supplemental Section S6 explicitly use short-time density limits (not only the stationary-gate absorption mean and variance at one initial point); they do not provide this globally bijective two-moment image or the sharp variance feasibility floor. Best-of-knowledge originality survives, with cautious specialist-literature residual risk.

value.rationale: An experimentally natural inverse problem is reduced from a full distribution to two low-order time statistics, and an exact attainable region plus sharp unrealizable boundary is proved for the nontrivial coupled-boundary model. Exact structural identifiability and feasibility can inform inverse diffusion studies even if noisy statistical conditioning is not covered.

final_claim: For D,L>0, stationary two-state gate and Brownian motion starting at reflecting x=L with absorption at open x=0, positive gate rates alpha,beta are uniquely recovered from dimensionless mean m and variance v exactly when m>1/2 and v>m^2-m/3+1/12.
